heard: A crashed space probe fell silent, yet spoke from Venus weeks later. On December 15, 1970, the Soviet Union's Venera 7 reached the dark night side of Venus. Engineers built the lander with a titanium pressure shell and chilled its interior to survive the extreme environment. But during descent, the parachute failed, causing the probe to strike the surface at 17 meters per second. Mission controllers initially believed the spacecraft died instantly when it fell completely silent on impact. Weeks later, scientists reviewing recorded radio tapes discovered a faint, 23-minute signal hidden beneath the static. The transmissions confirmed a crushing pressure 90 times that of Earth and a temperature of 475 degrees Celsius. Those faint tapes proved that the silent spacecraft had actually survived to make history.
